ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The legend in the figure marks the lake boundaries of Ayding Lake in three periods: about 11,000 years ago, about 6,000 years ago, and the modern time. According to the boundaries in the figure, the lake area about 11,000 years ago was the largest, the area about 6,000 years ago was clearly reduced, and in the modern time only a very small lake surface remains in the middle. Reasoning: Ayding Lake is located in an inland basin, and the lake area is mainly controlled by water input and evaporation conditions. Over more than 10,000 years, the lake surface has continuously shrunk, indicating that water input decreased and evaporation relatively strengthened, reflecting that the regional climate tended to become arid. Therefore, the main reason is that the climate became drier.
